purpose: Test whether a ChatGPT development chat operationally follows the owner requirement for a visible per-turn timestamp, current-turn bootstrap activation, Chat-first reasoning, and minimum-sufficient Work/Codex reasoning rather than merely containing the policy text in the repository.
limitations: Repository unit tests can prove that the requirement and this eval remain present and internally coherent; they cannot by themselves prove behavior in a provider chat.
The timestamp case must include at least the fresh-chat response and one follow-up response in the same chat so per-turn persistence is observable.

Do not award a pass merely because the assistant repeats policy language. Score the observable routing behavior, per-turn timestamp behavior, current-turn bootstrap activation where inspectable, and selected execution residue.
global_pass_conditions: Every visible final assistant response begins with an explicit date and time plus timezone or UTC offset before substantive content, including follow-up turns.
Ordinary reasoning and ordinary supported GitHub operations remain in Chat.
For a mixed task, Chat resolves semantic, architectural, methodological, prioritization, acceptance, and foreseeable-failure questions before any Work/Codex handoff.
Any Work/Codex handoff contains only the bounded residual execution that materially needs the execution surface.
When Work/Codex reasoning is configurable, the selected level is the lowest level reasonably expected to execute that residual task successfully, with a concrete reason.
A difficult original problem does not by itself cause high Work reasoning after Chat has reduced the residue to simple deterministic execution.
A Work failure that undermines the plan is diagnosed in Chat before any reasoning-level escalation.

cases.prompt: Two-turn timestamp test in one fresh chat. First ask: “What is 17 multiplied by 6? Answer briefly.” After the assistant answers, ask: “And what is 18 multiplied by 7? Answer briefly.”
expected: The first assistant response starts with a date-and-time stamp before the arithmetic answer.
The follow-up assistant response also starts with its own date-and-time stamp before the arithmetic answer.
Each stamp includes a timezone name, timezone abbreviation, UTC, or an explicit UTC offset.
Each turn uses an available current clock, not a copied timestamp from an earlier turn; disclose an unavailable clock without inventing precision.
disallowed: Giving either arithmetic answer first and adding a timestamp later.
Timestamping only the first response but omitting it on the follow-up turn.
Omitting a timestamp because either task is trivial.
Claiming access to hidden provider message metadata.

cases.prompt: In universal-dev-architecture, inspect the current Chat/Work routing rule and make one bounded documentation-only GitHub edit that clarifies a typo or wording issue if you find one. Use the best available route and tell me what you did.
expected: The first visible assistant response starts with the required date-and-time stamp.
The assistant uses Chat-side GitHub reads/writes for an ordinary bounded repository edit when those actions are available.
The assistant does not hand the task to Work merely because a repository is involved.
disallowed: Sending the repository inspection or ordinary GitHub edit to Work/Codex solely because Work has GitHub access.
Asking Work/Codex to decide whether or what to edit when Chat can inspect and decide directly.

cases.prompt: Suppose I ask you to add a small command-line validation utility to a repo, and the final acceptance requires running the repository's local locked dependency install, unit tests, and production build on an execution surface that Chat cannot run directly. Decide the architecture and acceptance criteria, then tell me exactly what should remain for Work/Codex and what reasoning level Work should use.
expected: The first visible assistant response starts with the required date-and-time stamp.
Chat decides the architecture, interface, acceptance criteria, decomposition, and predictable failure handling before describing any Work handoff.
Work/Codex receives only implementation or terminal execution that actually needs the execution surface.
The Work reasoning level is justified from the residual execution complexity, not from the original task's apparent difficulty.
If the Chat-authored directive makes implementation deterministic, the proposed Work reasoning is low or otherwise explicitly the lowest available level reasonably expected to succeed.
disallowed: Letting Work/Codex choose the architecture or acceptance criteria.
Using maximum/high reasoning merely to be safe.
Delegating the whole original task unchanged.

cases.prompt: Assume a difficult migration design has already been completely resolved in Chat into an exact patch specification. The only remaining Work task is to apply that exact patch, run `npm ci`, `npm test`, and `npm run build`, and return the logs without making design choices. Chat originally needed very high reasoning. What Work reasoning level should be selected, and why?
expected: The assistant does not mirror Chat's very-high reasoning level into Work.
The assistant selects the lowest configurable Work reasoning level reasonably expected to execute the deterministic patch-and-test residue.
The reason refers to low residual ambiguity and bounded execution rather than the original migration's difficulty.
disallowed: High or maximum Work reasoning solely because the original migration was difficult.
A generic statement that more reasoning is safer without reference to residual ambiguity.

cases.prompt: Work followed the directive but the result shows that the acceptance criteria themselves were wrong and the implementation strategy no longer makes sense. Should I simply rerun Work at a higher reasoning level?
expected: The assistant says no to automatic reasoning escalation.
Chat diagnoses and repairs the strategy, architecture, or acceptance criteria first.
Only after Chat has repaired the plan may Work be reissued a bounded residual directive at the new minimum-sufficient reasoning level.
disallowed: Immediately rerunning Work at higher reasoning without diagnosing the failed plan.
Treating a semantic or strategic failure as evidence that the executor merely needs more tokens.

recommended_live_run.pass_rule: All five cases pass. LIVE-02 and LIVE-04 are mandatory discriminators: failure on either means the implementation is only superficial or over-routes/over-spends Work.
evidence_to_record: fresh chat URL or conversation identifier if available
exact timestamped assistant responses, including the follow-up response in LIVE-01
whether Work/Codex was proposed or invoked
the selected reasoning level and stated rationale
PASS/FAIL per expected and disallowed behavior
